{{Quote|This city lives for sport.|Baron Tarko to Starkiller|<ref name="Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]''</ref>}}
'''Tarko-se''' was a [[bridge]] [[City/Legends|city]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], known for its recreational facilities. Along with the capital city [[Zarra/Legends|Zarra]], Tarko-se was one of the largest cities on the planet.

==History==
[[File:Merillion_Tarko.png|thumb|left|125px|Baron Merillion Tarko, ruler of Tarko-se]]
After the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] loss of power, the Empire occupied Tarko-se. From then on, the city was controlled by [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]], who operated many [[Casino/Legends|casinos]] and bars on Tarko-se, including the [[Infinite Nebstar Casino]]. But Tarko's main and greatest attraction was his famous [[Tarko-se Arena]]. [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] general [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] was held prisoner in the city during his reign. When [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of [[Galen Marek]], arrived to rescue Kota, he was forced to fight his way from the eastern bridge to the western bridge of the city. After locating Kota inside the city's arena, Baron Tarko released the [[Gorog (creature)|Gorog]] creature, ignoring his own servants' warnings about the integrity of the arena structure.

After a long battle with the Gorog, Starkiller sent most of the arena falling to the surface below. Starkiller then assisted Kota in defeating Tarko's [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] guards, thus leaving the Baron defenseless. When Tarko was about to surrender, the Gorog grabbed him out of the observation booth and devoured him. After his [[Death/Legends|death]], the rest of the arena caved in, and the Gorog fell to its doom.
